# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by bin/generate-tool-docs.php — do not edit by hand. -->

Site Manager 0.4.1 exposes **209 tools** in 22 groups. Integration groups appear only when their plugin is active. Every tool requires the `manage_options` capability; a few also require the matching WordPress capability noted below.

Legend: **read** — no changes · **write** — changes the site · **destructive** — deletes or overwrites data (clients should confirm first) · **external** — contacts other servers or sends email · **gated** — off until enabled in Settings → Site Manager → Tools. Required parameters are in bold.

## Groups

- [Site overview](#site-overview) (3) — Site summary, Site Health report, search across all content.
- [Content](#content) (21) — Posts, pages and custom post types; custom fields (post meta); revisions; blocks.
- [Taxonomies](#taxonomies) (7) — Categories, tags, custom taxonomies, term meta.
- [Media](#media) (7) — Media library uploads, alt text, captions, image sizes.
- [Users & roles](#users--roles) (13) — User accounts, profile fields, user meta, roles and capabilities.
- [Comments](#comments) (6) — Read, reply to and moderate comments.
- [Settings & options](#settings--options) (6) — Settings screens (general, reading, discussion, media, permalinks) and any option in the options table.
- [Menus & widgets](#menus--widgets) (10) — Navigation menus, menu items, menu locations, sidebars and widgets.
- [Appearance](#appearance) (11) — Themes, customizer settings, additional CSS, global styles.
- [Plugins & updates](#plugins--updates) (10) — Install, activate, deactivate, update and delete plugins; core, plugin and theme updates.
- [Maintenance](#maintenance) (8) — Scheduled tasks (cron), cache and transient flushing, rewrite rules, test email, debug log.
- [Developer](#developer) (12) — Internal REST API passthrough, database queries, theme/plugin files, hooks, PHP execution.
- [Activity log](#activity-log) (3) — Search the site-wide audit log and build activity reports.

- [Advanced Custom Fields](#advanced-custom-fields) (9) — ACF field groups, field values on posts/terms/users/options, ACF post types and taxonomies.
- [Yoast SEO](#yoast-seo) (8) — SEO titles, meta descriptions, focus keyphrases, robots, social metadata, Yoast settings.
- [WooCommerce](#woocommerce) (22) — Products, variations, stock, orders, refunds, customers, coupons, sales reports.
- [Gravity Forms](#gravity-forms) (11) — Forms, fields, notifications, confirmations and entries.

## Site overview

Site summary, Site Health report, search across all content.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `site_info` | read | — | Overview of the site: name, URLs, WordPress/PHP/database versions, active theme, active plugins, post types, taxonomies, content counts, permalink structure, timezone, multisite and debug flags, and which integrations (ACF, Yoast, WooCommerce, Gravity Forms, WPForms, Contact Form 7, Redirection, Elementor) are active. Call this first. |
| `site_health` | read | sections | The full Site Health "Info" report (server, database, constants, filesystem permissions, media handling, theme and plugins). Pass sections to limit output, e.g. ["wp-server","wp-database","wp-constants"]. |
| `site_search` | read | **query**, limit | Search titles and content across every post type (including drafts and private), plus terms and users, in one call. |

## Content

Posts, pages and custom post types; custom fields (post meta); revisions; blocks.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `post_types_list` | read | include_internal | List registered post types (built-in and custom) with labels, supported features, taxonomies, hierarchy and post counts. |
| `post_list` | read | post_type, status, search, author, parent, include, slug, tax_query, meta_query, after, before, orderby, order, meta_key, page, per_page | Query posts of any post type with filters for status, search, author, parent, taxonomy terms, meta values and dates. Returns summaries; use post_get for full details. |
| `post_get` | read | id, url, post_type, slug, include_content, include_meta, include_private_meta | Get one post of any type with content, terms, featured image, custom fields (meta), ACF values and Yoast SEO data. Look up by id, by url, or by post_type + slug. |
| `post_create` | write | post_type, **title**, content, excerpt, status, slug, date, author, parent, menu_order, comment_status, ping_status, password, template, featured_image_id, terms, terms_append, meta, acf, yoast | Create a post of any type (post, page, or custom post type) and in the same call set its terms, custom fields, ACF fields, Yoast SEO fields, featured image and template. Defaults to status=draft. |
| `post_update` | write | **id**, title, content, excerpt, status, slug, date, author, parent, menu_order, comment_status, ping_status, password, template, featured_image_id, terms, terms_append, meta, acf, yoast | Update any post. Only the fields you pass are changed. Can also set terms, custom fields, ACF fields, Yoast SEO fields, featured image and template. |
| `post_delete` | write, destructive | **id**, force, dry_run | Move a post to the trash, or permanently delete it with force=true. |
| `post_restore` | write | **id** | Restore a trashed post. |
| `post_duplicate` | write | **id**, title, status | Duplicate a post (content, terms, meta, featured image) as a new draft. |
| `posts_bulk_update` | write | **ids**, status, author, parent, comment_status, terms, terms_append, meta, dry_run | Apply the same change to many posts: status, author, parent, comment_status, terms (replace or append), or meta. |
| `content_search_replace` | write, destructive | **search**, **replace**, regex, post_type, fields, status, limit, dry_run | Find and replace text in post titles, content and excerpts across post types. Runs as a dry run by default and reports matches; pass dry_run=false to apply. Does not touch meta or options (use db tools for serialized data). |
| `post_meta_get` | read | **id**, key, include_private | Read custom fields (post meta) for a post — all keys, or one key. Includes protected underscore keys when asked. |
| `post_meta_update` | write | **id**, **meta**, add | Set custom fields (post meta) on a post. Pass a {key: value} map; null deletes a key. For multi-value keys use add=true to add a value instead of replacing. |
| `post_meta_delete` | write, destructive | **id**, **key**, value | Delete a meta key from a post (all values, or only rows matching value). |
| `meta_keys_list` | read | post_type, include_private, search | Discover custom fields: distinct meta keys in use for a post type (with usage counts and a sample value), plus keys formally registered with register_meta(). |
| `revisions_list` | read | **id** | List revisions of a post (newest first). |
| `revision_get` | read | **revision_id** | Get a revision's full title, content and excerpt. |
| `revision_restore` | write | **revision_id** | Restore a post to a previous revision. |
| `post_blocks_get` | read | **id** | Parse a post's content into a Gutenberg block tree (blockName, attrs, innerHTML, innerBlocks) — useful for precise edits. |
| `post_blocks_update` | write | **id**, **blocks** | Replace a post's content with a block tree (same shape post_blocks_get returns). Serialized with WordPress's own serializer. |
| `block_types_list` | read | search, include_attributes | List registered block types (core and plugin blocks) with title, category and optionally their attribute schemas. |
| `block_patterns_list` | read | name, search | List registered block patterns. Pass name to get one pattern's content. |

## Taxonomies

Categories, tags, custom taxonomies, term meta.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `taxonomies_list` | read | include_internal | List registered taxonomies (built-in and custom) with the post types they apply to, hierarchy and term counts. |
| `terms_list` | read | **taxonomy**, search, parent, hide_empty, orderby, order, page, per_page | List terms in a taxonomy, with optional search, parent filter and pagination. |
| `term_get` | read | id, taxonomy, slug | Get a term with its meta (and ACF / Yoast values when those plugins are active). Look up by id, or by taxonomy + slug. |
| `term_create` | write | **taxonomy**, **name**, slug, description, parent, meta, acf, yoast | Create a term in any taxonomy. |
| `term_update` | write | **id**, name, slug, description, parent, meta, acf, yoast | Update a term's name, slug, description, parent, meta, ACF or Yoast fields. |
| `term_delete` | write, destructive | **id**, dry_run | Delete a term. Posts keep existing; they just lose the term. |
| `post_terms_set` | write | **post_id**, **taxonomy**, **terms**, mode | Set (or append / remove) a post's terms in one taxonomy. Terms can be IDs or names; unknown names are created when adding. |

## Media

Media library uploads, alt text, captions, image sizes.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media_list` | read | mime_type, search, parent, missing_alt, after, before, page, per_page | List media library items, filtered by MIME type, search term, attached post or date. |
| `media_get` | read | **id** | Get a media item's URL, file name, dimensions, generated sizes, alt text, caption and description. |
| `media_upload` | write, external | url, data, filename, title, alt, caption, description, post_id, set_featured | Add a file to the media library from a public URL or base64 data. Optionally set title, alt text, caption, description, attach it to a post, or make it that post's featured image. |
| `media_update` | write | **id**, title, alt, caption, description, parent | Update a media item's title, alt text, caption, description or attached post. |
| `media_delete` | write, destructive | **id**, dry_run | Permanently delete a media item and its files. |
| `media_regenerate` | write | **ids** | Regenerate thumbnails / image sizes for one or more images. |
| `image_sizes_list` | read | — | List registered image sizes with dimensions and crop settings. |

## Users & roles

User accounts, profile fields, user meta, roles and capabilities.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `users_list` | read | role, search, meta_key, meta_value, orderby, order, page, per_page | List users, filtered by role, search (login, email, URL, name) or meta. |
| `user_get` | read | id, username, email, include_private | Get a user by id, username or email, including profile fields, roles, capabilities, post count and meta. |
| `user_create` | write | **username**, password, notify, **email**, first_name, last_name, display_name, nickname, url, description, role, locale, meta, acf | Create a user. A strong password is generated if none is given. Optionally email the new user their login details. |
| `user_update` | write | **id**, password, email, first_name, last_name, display_name, nickname, url, description, role, locale, meta, acf | Update a user's profile fields, role, password, meta or ACF fields. |
| `user_delete` | write, destructive | **id**, reassign_to, dry_run | Delete a user. Their content is reassigned to reassign_to, or deleted if reassign_to is omitted. You cannot delete yourself. |
| `user_send_password_reset` | write, external | **id** | Email a user a password-reset link. |
| `user_sessions_destroy` | write | **id** | Log a user out everywhere by destroying all of their sessions. |
| `roles_list` | read | include_capabilities | List roles with their capabilities and user counts. |
| `role_create` | write | **role**, **name**, clone_from, capabilities | Create a role, optionally cloning capabilities from an existing role. |
| `role_update` | write | **role**, add, remove | Add or remove capabilities on a role. Removing capabilities from administrator is refused. |
| `role_delete` | write, destructive | **role** | Delete a custom role. Users with only that role are moved to the default role. |
| `application_passwords_list` | read | **user_id** | List a user's application passwords (names, created and last-used dates — never the passwords). |
| `application_password_revoke` | write, destructive | **user_id**, **uuid** | Revoke one of a user's application passwords by uuid. |

## Comments

Read, reply to and moderate comments.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `comments_list` | read | status, post_id, type, search, page, per_page | List comments by status (hold = pending, approve, spam, trash, all), post, type or search term. Includes counts per status. |
| `comment_get` | read | **id** | Get a single comment with its meta. |
| `comment_create` | write | **post_id**, **content**, parent | Post a comment or reply as the connected admin. Approved immediately. |
| `comment_update` | write | **id**, content, status, author, author_email, author_url | Edit a comment's content or author fields, or moderate it by setting status (approve, hold, spam, trash). |
| `comments_moderate` | write | **ids**, **status** | Set the status of many comments at once (approve, hold, spam, trash). |
| `comment_delete` | write, destructive | **id** | Permanently delete a comment (use comment_update status=trash to trash it instead). |

## Settings & options

Settings screens (general, reading, discussion, media, permalinks) and any option in the options table.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `settings_get` | read | group | Read WordPress settings grouped by Settings screen: general, writing, reading, discussion, media, permalinks, privacy. Omit group for all. |
| `settings_update` | write | **settings**, confirm_url_change | Update core settings by option name, e.g. {"blogname": "Acme", "posts_per_page": 12, "show_on_front": "page", "page_on_front": 42}. Only options on the core Settings screens are accepted; use option_update for anything else. Changing permalink_structure flushes rewrite rules. siteurl/home require confirm_url_change=true. |
| `options_list` | read | search, include_transients, autoload_only, page, per_page | Search the options table by name (SQL LIKE pattern or substring). Returns names, autoload flag and value size — use option_get for values. Useful for finding plugin settings. |
| `option_get` | read | **names** | Read one or more options by name. Serialized values are returned as JSON. |
| `option_update` | write | **name**, **value**, merge, autoload, confirm | Create or update any option. For array options, set merge=true to merge keys into the existing value instead of replacing it. Changing siteurl, home, active_plugins, template or stylesheet requires confirm=true. |
| `option_delete` | write, destructive | **name**, confirm | Delete an option. |

## Menus & widgets

Navigation menus, menu items, menu locations, sidebars and widgets.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `menus_list` | read | — | List classic navigation menus, registered theme menu locations, and which menu is assigned to each location. (Block themes also store navigation in wp_navigation posts — see post_list post_type=wp_navigation.) |
| `menu_get` | read | **menu** | Get a menu and its items as a nested tree. |
| `menu_create` | write | **name**, locations | Create a menu, optionally assigning it to theme locations. |
| `menu_update` | write | **menu**, **name** | Rename a menu. |
| `menu_delete` | write, destructive | **menu** | Delete a menu and all its items. |
| `menu_item_add` | write | **menu**, title, **type**, object, object_id, url, parent_id, position, target, classes, attr_title, description, xfn | Add an item to a menu: a page/post (type=post_type), a term (type=taxonomy), or a custom URL (type=custom). |
| `menu_item_update` | write | **item_id**, title, type, object, object_id, url, parent_id, position, target, classes, attr_title, description, xfn | Update a menu item (label, link, parent, position, classes…). Only the fields you pass change. |
| `menu_item_delete` | write, destructive | **item_id** | Remove an item from a menu. |
| `menu_locations_set` | write | **locations** | Assign menus to theme locations: {"primary": 12, "footer": 0}. 0 unassigns. |
| `sidebars_list` | read | — | List registered widget areas (sidebars) and the widgets in each, with their settings. Edit widgets via rest_request on /wp/v2/widgets. |

## Appearance

Themes, customizer settings, additional CSS, global styles.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `themes_list` | read | — | List installed themes with version, parent theme, whether it's active, a block theme, and has an update available. |
| `theme_activate` | write, destructive | **stylesheet** | Switch the active theme. Changes the whole front end — confirm with the user first. |
| `theme_install` | write, external, needs `install_themes` | slug, zip_url, activate | Install a theme from WordPress.org by slug, or from a zip URL. Optionally activate it. |
| `theme_update` | write, external, needs `update_themes` | **stylesheet** | Update an installed theme to the latest available version. |
| `theme_delete` | write, destructive, needs `delete_themes` | **stylesheet** | Delete an installed (inactive) theme. |
| `theme_mods_get` | read | — | Read the active theme's customizer settings (theme mods): logo, header, colors, menu locations, theme-specific options. |
| `theme_mods_update` | write | **mods** | Set customizer settings (theme mods) on the active theme: {"custom_logo": 12, "header_textcolor": "000000"}. null removes a mod. |
| `custom_css_get` | read | — | Get the Additional CSS for the active theme. |
| `custom_css_update` | write | **css**, append | Replace the Additional CSS for the active theme (or append with append=true). |
| `global_styles_get` | read | include_merged | Block themes: get the user global styles (Site Editor → Styles) and the merged theme.json settings for colors, typography and spacing. |
| `global_styles_update` | write | **styles** | Block themes: replace the user global styles JSON ({"version": 3, "settings": {...}, "styles": {...}}). Get the current value first and modify it. |

## Plugins & updates

Install, activate, deactivate, update and delete plugins; core, plugin and theme updates.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins_list` | read | status | List installed plugins (including must-use and drop-ins) with version, active status, available updates and auto-update status. |
| `plugin_search` | read, external | **search**, per_page | Search the WordPress.org plugin directory. |
| `plugin_activate` | write, needs `activate_plugins` | **plugins** | Activate one or more installed plugins. |
| `plugin_deactivate` | write, destructive, needs `activate_plugins` | **plugins** | Deactivate one or more plugins. Site Manager itself cannot be deactivated this way. |
| `plugin_install` | write, external, needs `install_plugins` | slug, zip_url, activate | Install a plugin from WordPress.org by slug, or from a zip URL. Optionally activate it. |
| `plugin_update` | write, external, needs `update_plugins` | **plugins** | Update one or more plugins to their latest versions. |
| `plugin_delete` | write, destructive, needs `delete_plugins` | **plugins** | Delete plugins (deactivating them first). Runs their uninstall routines, which may remove their data. |
| `plugin_auto_update_set` | write | **plugins**, **enabled** | Enable or disable automatic updates for plugins. |
| `updates_check` | read, external | — | Check WordPress.org for available core, plugin, theme and translation updates. |
| `core_update` | write, destructive, external, needs `update_core` | **confirm** | Update WordPress core to the latest offered version. Take a backup first and confirm with the user. |

## Maintenance

Scheduled tasks (cron), cache and transient flushing, rewrite rules, test email, debug log.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cron_list` | read | hook | List scheduled cron events (hook, next run, schedule, args) and the available schedules. |
| `cron_run` | write | **hook**, args | Run a cron hook immediately (fires its callbacks now with the given args). Does not change its schedule. |
| `cron_unschedule` | write, destructive | **hook**, args | Remove every scheduled occurrence of a cron hook (optionally only those with matching args). |
| `cache_flush` | write | — | Flush the object cache, and — when known caching plugins are active — their page caches (WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, LiteSpeed, SiteGround, WP Fastest Cache, Autoptimize). |
| `transients_delete` | write | scope, name | Delete expired transients (default), all transients, or a single transient by name. |
| `rewrite_flush` | write | hard | Flush rewrite rules (fixes 404s on custom post types / after permalink changes). |
| `email_send` | write, external | **to**, **subject**, **body**, html | Send an email through WordPress (wp_mail) — e.g. to test that site email works. Confirm recipients with the user first. |
| `debug_log_read` | read | lines, filter | Read the last lines of the PHP / WordPress debug log (wp-content/debug.log or the WP_DEBUG_LOG path), optionally filtered. |

## Developer

Internal REST API passthrough, database queries, theme/plugin files, hooks, PHP execution.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rest_routes_list` | read | namespace | List REST API namespaces, or the routes and methods within one namespace (e.g. "wp/v2", "wc/v3", "gf/v2", "elementor/v1"). Use with rest_request to reach any plugin that has a REST API. |
| `rest_request` | write | method, **route**, query, body, embed | Call any WordPress REST API route internally, as the connected administrator — no extra auth needed. Covers core endpoints (/wp/v2/widgets, /wp/v2/templates, /wp/v2/settings…) and every plugin's routes (WooCommerce /wc/v3, Gravity Forms /gf/v2, etc). |
| `db_tables_list` | read | describe | List database tables with row counts, sizes and engine. Optionally show one table's columns and indexes. |
| `db_query` | read | **sql**, max_rows | Run a read-only SQL query (SELECT, SHOW, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN) in a read-only transaction. Use {prefix} for the table prefix, e.g. "SELECT * FROM {prefix}posts LIMIT 5". |
| `db_execute` | write, destructive, gated (database writes) | **sql** | Run a write SQL statement (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, REPLACE, ALTER, CREATE, DROP, TRUNCATE). {prefix} is replaced with the table prefix. Take care with serialized PHP values. Confirm with the user before running. |
| `file_list` | read | path, recursive | List files and folders under a path relative to the WordPress root (e.g. "wp-content/themes/my-theme"). |
| `file_read` | read | **path**, start_line, end_line | Read a text file under the WordPress root (theme templates, plugin code, .htaccess, logs). wp-config.php and .env files are never readable. Max 1 MB. |
| `file_write` | write, destructive, gated (file writes) | **path**, **content** | Create or overwrite a file inside wp-content (e.g. a child theme template or functions.php). PHP files are syntax-checked first when possible. A .bak copy of the previous version is kept. |
| `file_delete` | write, destructive, gated (file writes) | **path** | Delete a file inside wp-content. |
| `hooks_list` | read | hook, search | Show the callbacks attached to an action or filter (priority, function, file:line) — useful for debugging what a plugin or theme changes. Pass search instead to find hook names. |
| `shortcodes_list` | read | — | List registered shortcodes and the callbacks that render them. |
| `php_execute` | write, destructive, gated (php execution) | **code** | Evaluate PHP code inside WordPress (no opening <?php tag). Echoed output and the return value are captured. Full server access — use only when no dedicated tool fits, and confirm with the user first. |

## Activity log

Search the site-wide audit log and build activity reports.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activity_log_query` | read | after, before, user, category, action, severity, min_severity, source, object_type, object_id, ip, search, order, page, per_page | Search the activity log, newest first. Filter by date range, user, category (auth, user, plugin, theme, core, post, media, taxonomy, menu, comment, setting, file, export, privacy, mcp, site_manager, woocommerce, form, redirect), action (e.g. login_failed, plugin_updated, published), severity, source (admin, rest, mcp, cron, cli, login, web, ajax, xmlrpc), object, IP or free text. Repeated events (e.g. failed-login floods) are folded into one row with an occurrences count. |
| `activity_report` | read | after, before, month | Summarize activity for a period — defaults to last calendar month. Returns: core/plugin/theme/translation updates with old → new versions and whether automatic, failed updates; plugins and themes installed/activated/deactivated/deleted/switched; users created/deleted/role changes/password changes; successful logins by user and failed logins by username and IP; content changes by post type; settings changes; all warning/critical security events; MCP tool usage; WooCommerce order status changes and refunds; and totals by category, severity and source. Use this to write monthly client reports and security audits. |
| `activity_stats` | read | group_by, after, before, category, action, min_severity, limit | Count activity grouped by a dimension (category, action, user_login, source, severity, ip, object_type, object_name, or day) for a period and optional filters — e.g. "failed logins per IP this week" or "content updates per day". |

## Client reports

Branded monthly PDF reports: settings, generation, archive and email delivery.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `report_settings_get` | read | — | Get the client report settings: title, agency name/website/contact, logo, accent color, paper size, intro text, sections, recipients, email subject, reply-to and monthly schedule. |
| `report_settings_update` | write | title, agency_name, agency_url, agency_contact, logo_id, accent_color, paper, intro, sections, recipients, subject, reply_to, schedule, send_day | Update client report settings. Only fields you pass change. Subject supports {title}, {site}, {period} and {agency}. |
| `report_generate` | write | month, after, before, note, include_pdf | Generate the branded PDF report for a month (default: last month) or date range and save it to the report archive. Returns the report data (updates, plugin changes, content, users and logins, security events, store sales, form submissions, health) plus the archive ID for report_send. Set include_pdf=true to also get the PDF as base64. |
| `report_send` | write, external | report_id, recipients, note, month, after, before | Email a report as a PDF attachment. Pass report_id (from report_generate or reports_list), or a month/range to generate and send in one step. Uses the saved recipients unless recipients is given. Confirm recipients with the user first. |
| `reports_list` | read | — | List archived reports (newest first) with period, when generated, who received them and a wp-admin download link. |

## Advanced Custom Fields

ACF field groups, field values on posts/terms/users/options, ACF post types and taxonomies.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `acf_field_groups_list` | read | object | List ACF field groups with key, title, location rules, active state and field count. Pass object to list only the groups that apply to that post/term/user. |
| `acf_field_group_get` | read | **key** | Get a field group's full definition — every field (name, key, type, choices, sub-fields, layouts, conditional logic) in ACF's export format. Read this before writing values so you know field names and types. |
| `acf_field_group_save` | write | **group** | Create or update a field group from ACF's export JSON (title, fields, location, etc.). Matching key updates the existing group. Fields need unique keys (field_…); new keys are generated when missing. |
| `acf_field_group_delete` | write, destructive | **key** | Delete a field group and its field definitions. Stored values remain in the database. |
| `acf_values_get` | read | **object**, formatted | Get all ACF field values for an object (post, term, user, options page), with each field's type, label and key. Set formatted=true for display-ready values (expanded images, post objects). |
| `acf_values_update` | write | **object**, **values** | Set ACF field values on an object. Keys are field names or keys. Use raw values: attachment IDs for image/file/gallery, post IDs for post_object/relationship, term IDs for taxonomy, arrays of row objects (keyed by sub-field name) for repeaters / flexible content (include "acf_fc_layout" per row), an object for groups. null clears a field. |
| `acf_options_pages_list` | read | — | List ACF options pages (PRO) with their post_id, which you pass as object to acf_values_get / acf_values_update. |
| `acf_post_types_list` | read | — | List post types and taxonomies registered through ACF's UI (ACF 6.1+), with their full settings. |
| `acf_post_type_save` | write | **kind**, **config** | Create or update a post type or taxonomy registered through ACF (ACF 6.1+), using ACF's export format. kind = post_type \| taxonomy. |

## Yoast SEO

SEO titles, meta descriptions, focus keyphrases, robots, social metadata, Yoast settings.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yoast_post_get` | read | **id** | Get Yoast SEO data for a post: stored SEO fields, SEO and readability scores, primary terms, and the resolved title/description/canonical/robots that Yoast outputs in the page head. |
| `yoast_post_update` | write | **id**, title, description, focus_keyphrase, canonical, noindex, nofollow, robots_advanced, breadcrumb_title, og_title, og_description, og_image, og_image_id, twitter_title, twitter_description, twitter_image, twitter_image_id, cornerstone, schema_page_type, schema_article_type, primary_terms | Set Yoast SEO fields on a post (title, meta description, focus keyphrase, canonical, robots, social, schema, primary terms). Empty string clears a field. |
| `yoast_posts_audit` | read | post_type, issue, page, per_page | Find published posts with SEO gaps: missing meta description, missing focus keyphrase, noindex set, or low SEO score. Good for bulk SEO work. |
| `yoast_term_get` | read | **id** | Get Yoast SEO fields for a category, tag or custom taxonomy term. |
| `yoast_term_update` | write | **id**, title, description, focus_keyphrase, canonical, noindex, breadcrumb_title, og_title, og_description, og_image, og_image_id, twitter_title, twitter_description, twitter_image, twitter_image_id, cornerstone | Set Yoast SEO fields on a term. noindex takes default \| index \| noindex. |
| `yoast_settings_get` | read | option | Read Yoast settings. wpseo = features and site basics; wpseo_titles = title/description templates per post type, taxonomy and archive, separator, schema defaults, noindex defaults; wpseo_social = social profiles and default images. |
| `yoast_settings_update` | write | **option**, **values** | Update Yoast settings keys in one option group, e.g. option=wpseo_titles values={"title-post": "%%title%% %%sep%% %%sitename%%", "metadesc-page": "%%excerpt%%"}. Only existing keys are accepted. |
| `yoast_redirects_list` | read | — | List Yoast Premium redirects. |

## WooCommerce

Products, variations, stock, orders, refunds, customers, coupons, sales reports.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wc_store_info` | read | — | WooCommerce overview: version, currency, base location, tax and unit settings, store pages, enabled payment gateways, shipping zones, product counts and order counts by status. |
| `wc_products_list` | read | search, status, type, category, tag, sku, stock_status, on_sale, featured, orderby, order, page, per_page | List products with price, SKU, stock and categories. Filter by search, status, type, category, tag, SKU, stock status or on-sale. |
| `wc_product_get` | read | id, sku | Get a product (by id or sku) with full details: pricing, inventory, shipping, attributes, images, categories, linked products, and every variation of a variable product. |
| `wc_product_create` | write | **name**, type, status, slug, description, short_description, sku, regular_price, sale_price, date_on_sale_from, date_on_sale_to, manage_stock, stock_quantity, stock_status, backorders, low_stock_amount, sold_individually, weight, length, width, height, tax_status, tax_class, shipping_class_id, virtual, downloadable, featured, catalog_visibility, reviews_allowed, purchase_note, menu_order, categories, tags, image_id, gallery_image_ids, attributes, default_attributes, upsell_ids, cross_sell_ids, product_url, button_text, children, meta | Create a product (simple, variable, grouped or external). For variable products, set attributes with variation=true, then add variations with wc_variation_save. |
| `wc_product_update` | write | **id**, name, status, slug, description, short_description, sku, regular_price, sale_price, date_on_sale_from, date_on_sale_to, manage_stock, stock_quantity, stock_status, backorders, low_stock_amount, sold_individually, weight, length, width, height, tax_status, tax_class, shipping_class_id, virtual, downloadable, featured, catalog_visibility, reviews_allowed, purchase_note, menu_order, categories, tags, image_id, gallery_image_ids, attributes, default_attributes, upsell_ids, cross_sell_ids, product_url, button_text, children, meta | Update a product. Only the fields you pass change. |
| `wc_product_delete` | write, destructive | **id**, force | Trash a product or variation, or delete it permanently with force=true (also deletes a variable product's variations). |
| `wc_variation_save` | write | **product_id**, variation_id, attributes, status, sku, regular_price, sale_price, manage_stock, stock_quantity, stock_status, weight, length, width, height, image_id, description, virtual, downloadable | Create (omit variation_id) or update a variation of a variable product. attributes maps attribute name → option, e.g. {"pa_color":"Blue","Size":"M"}; omit an attribute to mean "any". |
| `wc_stock_update` | write | **items** | Set or adjust stock for many products/variations at once, identified by id or sku. mode: set (default), increase, decrease. |
| `wc_attributes_list` | read | — | List global product attributes (Products → Attributes) with their terms. |
| `wc_attribute_create` | write | **name**, slug, terms | Create a global product attribute (e.g. Color) and optionally its terms. |
| `wc_orders_list` | read | status, customer, after, before, page, per_page | List orders, newest first. Filter by status, customer (user ID or email), and date range. |
| `wc_order_get` | read | **id** | Get an order with line items, totals, taxes, shipping, coupons, addresses, payment details, refunds and order notes. |
| `wc_order_create` | write | customer_id, billing, shipping, **line_items**, shipping_lines, coupon_codes, status, payment_method, customer_note, set_paid | Create a manual order (like Orders → Add new). Totals are calculated from the products. Confirm details with the user first. |
| `wc_order_update` | write | **id**, status, note, note_to_customer, billing, shipping, customer_note, transaction_id, meta | Update an order: change status (which sends the normal customer emails), add a private or customer-facing note, edit addresses, customer note, transaction ID or meta. |
| `wc_order_refund` | write, destructive, external | **order_id**, amount, reason, refund_payment, restock_items | Refund an order (full or partial). By default only records the refund; refund_payment=true also refunds through the payment gateway (real money). Always confirm the amount with the user. |
| `wc_customers_list` | read | search, page, per_page | List registered customers with order count and total spent. |
| `wc_customer_get` | read | id, email | Get a customer (by user ID or email) with billing/shipping addresses, order count, total spent and recent orders. |
| `wc_customer_update` | write | **id**, first_name, last_name, email, billing, shipping | Update a customer's name, email, billing or shipping address. |
| `wc_coupons_list` | read | search, page, per_page | List coupons with type, amount, usage and expiry. |
| `wc_coupon_save` | write | id, code, discount_type, amount, description, date_expires, individual_use, free_shipping, exclude_sale_items, minimum_amount, maximum_amount, usage_limit, usage_limit_per_user, limit_usage_to_x_items, product_ids, excluded_product_ids, product_categories, excluded_product_categories, email_restrictions | Create a coupon (omit id) or update one. Only fields you pass change. |
| `wc_coupon_delete` | write, destructive | **id** | Delete a coupon permanently. |
| `wc_sales_report` | read | after, before, top | Sales summary for a date range: order count, gross and net sales, refunds, discounts, shipping, tax, items sold, average order value, daily totals and top products. Counts completed, processing and on-hold orders. |

## Gravity Forms

Forms, fields, notifications, confirmations and entries.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gf_forms_list` | read | include_inactive, include_trash | List Gravity Forms with ID, title, active state, field count, and entry counts (total / unread / starred). |
| `gf_form_get` | read | **id** | Get a form's full definition: fields (id, type, label, choices, required, conditional logic), notifications, confirmations and settings. Also returns a compact field map (id → label/type). |
| `gf_form_save` | write | **form** | Create a form (omit form.id) or update one by passing the complete form object, usually gf_form_get's output with changes. Minimal create: {"title":"Contact","fields":[{"id":1,"type":"name","label":"Name"},{"id":2,"type":"email","label":"Email","isRequired":true},{"id":3,"type":"textarea","label":"Message"}]}. |
| `gf_form_set_active` | write | **id**, **active** | Activate or deactivate a form. |
| `gf_form_delete` | write, destructive | **id**, **confirm** | Permanently delete a form and all of its entries. |
| `gf_entries_list` | read | form_id, status, search, field_filters, start_date, end_date, is_read, is_starred, page, per_page | List entries for a form (or all forms with form_id=0), newest first. Filter by status, date range, read/starred, free-text search, or specific field values. Values are keyed by field ID, with a labels map. |
| `gf_entry_get` | read | **id** | Get one entry with values labeled by field, plus its notes. |
| `gf_entry_create` | write | **form_id**, **values** | Add an entry directly (no notifications or add-on feeds run). values: {"1.3":"Jane","1.6":"Doe","2":"jane@example.com"}. |
| `gf_entry_update` | write | **id**, values, status, is_read, is_starred, note | Update an entry: field values, status (active / spam / trash), is_read, is_starred, or add a note. |
| `gf_entry_delete` | write, destructive | **id** | Permanently delete an entry (use gf_entry_update status=trash to trash it instead). |
| `gf_entry_resend_notifications` | write, external | **id**, notification_ids | Re-send a form's notifications for an entry (all, or the given notification IDs). |

## WPForms

WPForms forms (fields, notifications, confirmations) and Pro entries.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wpforms_forms_list` | read | — | List WPForms forms with ID, title, status, field count, shortcode and (Pro) entry count. |
| `wpforms_form_get` | read | **id** | Get a form's full data: fields (id, type, label, choices, required…), settings, notifications and confirmations. |
| `wpforms_form_save` | write | id, title, data | Create a form (omit id; title required) or update one with the full form data from wpforms_form_get. Field example: {"0":{"id":"0","type":"name","label":"Name","format":"simple","required":"1"},"1":{"id":"1","type":"email","label":"Email","required":"1"},"2":{"id":"2","type":"textarea","label":"Message"}}. |
| `wpforms_form_delete` | write, destructive | **id** | Permanently delete a form (and, on Pro, its entries). |
| `wpforms_entries_list` | read | **form_id**, page, per_page | WPForms Pro: list entries for a form, newest first, with field values labeled. |
| `wpforms_entry_get` | read | **id** | WPForms Pro: get one entry with all field values and metadata. |

## Redirection

Redirects, redirect groups, 404 log and redirect log.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `redirection_setup` | write | run | Report whether Redirection's database is installed and up to date. With run=true, performs the first-time install or pending database upgrade (same as the setup wizard in Tools → Redirection). |
| `redirection_list` | read | source, target, title, group_id, status, orderby, direction, page, per_page | List redirects with source, target, code, hit count and last access. Filter by source URL, target, title, group or status. |
| `redirection_create` | write | **source**, target, code, regex, ignore_case, ignore_trailing_slash, query, title, group_id, enabled | Create a redirect. For a 410 Gone (or other error) pass code=410 and no target. |
| `redirection_bulk_create` | write | **redirects** | Create many redirects at once, e.g. after a site migration: [{"source":"/a","target":"/b"},…]. Each item accepts the same fields as redirection_create. |
| `redirection_update` | write | **id**, source, target, code, regex, ignore_case, ignore_trailing_slash, query, title, group_id, enabled | Update a redirect. Only the fields you pass change; enabled=false disables it. |
| `redirection_delete` | write, destructive | **ids** | Delete redirects by ID. |
| `redirection_groups` | read | name | List redirect groups, or create one by passing name. |
| `redirection_404s` | read | grouped, url, page, per_page | Read the 404 log. By default grouped by URL with hit counts (most frequent first) — the best list of URLs that need redirects. Set grouped=false for individual hits with referrer and user agent. |
| `redirection_404s_clear` | write, destructive | url | Delete 404 log entries — all of them, or only those whose URL contains url. |
| `redirection_log` | read | url, page, per_page | Read the redirect log (redirects that fired), newest first. |
| `redirection_test_url` | read | **url** | Request a URL on this site without following redirects and report the status code and Location header — verifies a redirect actually works. |

## Elementor

Elementor page layouts, widgets, templates and global kit settings.

| Tool | Type | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `elementor_status` | read | — | Elementor overview: version, Pro status, active kit, number of pages built with Elementor, template counts by type. |
| `elementor_pages_list` | read | post_type, search, page, per_page | List posts/pages built with Elementor. |
| `elementor_document_get` | read | **id**, format | Get an Elementor document's element tree. format=outline (default) gives a compact tree of element IDs, types and text snippets; format=full returns the complete JSON including every setting. Also returns page settings. |
| `elementor_document_save` | write, destructive | **id**, **elements**, settings | Replace a document's whole element tree (and optionally page settings), turning on Elementor for the post if needed. Missing element IDs are generated. Prefer the element_* tools for small edits. |
| `elementor_element_get` | read | **id**, **element_id** | Get one element (and its children) by element ID. |
| `elementor_element_update` | write | **id**, **element_id**, **settings** | Change settings on one element without resending the page: settings are merged (null removes a key). E.g. {"title":"New heading"} on a heading widget, {"editor":"<p>…</p>"} on a text-editor widget, {"text":"Buy now","link":{"url":"/shop"}} on a button. |
| `elementor_element_insert` | write | **id**, parent_id, position, **element** | Insert an element (with any children) into a container/section/column, or at the top level when parent_id is omitted. position is a 0-based index (default: end). Example widget: {"elType":"widget","widgetType":"heading","settings":{"title":"Hello","header_size":"h2"}}. |
| `elementor_element_delete` | write, destructive | **id**, **element_id** | Remove an element (and its children) from a document. |
| `elementor_text_replace` | write, destructive | **search**, **replace**, ids, dry_run | Find and replace text inside Elementor widget settings (headings, text, buttons, links…) across one post or every Elementor document. Dry run by default. |
| `elementor_templates_list` | read | type | List saved Elementor templates (pages, sections, containers, headers, footers, popups…) with type. Edit them with the elementor_document_* / element_* tools using their ID. |
| `elementor_kit_get` | read | keys | Get the active kit's global settings: global colors, global fonts, typography, buttons, form fields, layout (content width, breakpoints), site identity and custom CSS. |
| `elementor_kit_update` | write | **settings** | Merge settings into the active kit (global colors, fonts, layout…). Arrays such as system_colors are replaced whole, so pass the full list. Regenerates CSS. |
| `elementor_widgets_list` | read | name, search | List registered widget types (name, title, categories). Pass name to get one widget's control definitions (setting keys, types, defaults, options). |
| `elementor_css_regenerate` | write | — | Clear Elementor's generated CSS and data caches (Tools → Regenerate CSS & Data). Fixes stale styling. |
